cards.headline: REFORMS: Oil output has grown by 600,000bpd since PIA — NNPC
cards.what_happened: NNPC Limited says Nigeria's crude oil output has risen by 600,000 barrels per day, from about 1.2 million bpd to 1.8 million bpd, since the Petroleum Industry Act reforms. Group CEO Bashir Bayo Ojulari made the disclosure at the 2026 ADIPEC conference in Abu Dhabi and set a target of two million bpd by 2027.
analysis: Why it matters: The production claims and investment figures are management statements from NNPC's CEO and are not independently verified in the article. They bear on public expectations for oil revenue and on the company's reported performance under the PIA.

cards.headline: CBN sets N15bn capital requirement for dollar stablecoin issuers
cards.what_happened: The Central Bank of Nigeria has set a N15 billion capital requirement for issuers of dollar-denominated stablecoins.
analysis: Why it matters: A minimum capital threshold for stablecoin issuers sets the financial base operators must hold before entering the Nigerian market, which affects who can issue dollar-linked digital assets locally.

cards.headline: Tinubu to commission multi-billion naira projects in Akwa Ibom
cards.what_happened: President Tinubu is set to commission eight projects in Akwa Ibom on Friday, 6 November 2026. Premium Times reports that the state government has not published the contract sums or procurement records for the projects.
key_facts: N59.65 billion was allocated to the terminal alone across four budget cycles, according to the paper's review of budget documents.
The Akwa Ibom state government has not published contract sums or procurement records for the projects.

cards.headline: Reps query JAMB over N3b pension payment, N710m computer spending
cards.what_happened: The House of Representatives has queried the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) over a N3 billion pension payment and N710 million spent on computers.
analysis: Why it matters: The query concerns public money spent by a federal agency, so the outcome will bear on how JAMB accounts for large payments and procurements.

cards.headline: $196m NIN funds unspent, FG seeks extension
cards.what_happened: The Federal Government has requested a further 12-month extension for Nigeria's $430 million digital identity project. About $196 million of its financing remains undisbursed, according to the report.
key_facts: The Federal Government has requested another 12-month extension of Nigeria's $430 million digital identity project.
Approximately $196m of the project's financing remains undisbursed.
analysis: Why it matters: Unspent funds on a large national digital identity project affect how public financing is deployed and how long delivery timelines run. The article text provided is truncated, so further detail on the causes of delay is not available.
